subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is homeostasis?
options: The breakdown of glucose for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: In a knee-jerk reflex, the effector that produces the response is a:
questions.explain: The effector is the muscle that contracts to produce the response, e.g. the leg muscle making the lower leg kick.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is associated with:
options: A complete lack of a pancreas
Too much insulin being produced from birth
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: Which statement about the nervous system is correct?
options: Its effects last for several days
It uses chemicals carried slowly in the blood
It uses fast electrical impulses along neurones
It is controlled by the kidneys
questions.explain: Nervous responses use fast electrical impulses and are short-lived, unlike slower hormonal responses.

questions.q: Why are there gaps (synapses) between neurones rather than them being directly joined?
options: So blood can flow between them
So chemicals can transmit the signal, allowing connections and control between neurones
So impulses can travel more slowly always
questions.explain: Synapses use neurotransmitters to pass signals, allowing flexible connections between many neurones.

questions.q: What does a receptor in the nervous system do?
options: Detects a stimulus such as light, heat or pressure
questions.explain: Receptors detect stimuli (changes in the environment) and convert them into electrical impulses.

questions.q: What is the main function of the fatty myelin sheath around many neurones?
options: To insulate the neurone and speed up the impulse
questions.explain: The myelin sheath insulates the neurone and increases the speed at which the electrical impulse travels.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, which hormone maintains the uterus lining in the second half of the cycle?
questions.explain: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterus lining; when its level falls, the lining breaks down and menstruation occurs.

questions.q: When you touch a hot object and pull your hand away before feeling pain, this shows that a reflex:
options: Happens before the brain consciously processes the pain
Is slower than a conscious response
questions.explain: The reflex (handled by the spinal cord) acts before the impulse reaches the conscious brain, so you react before feeling pain.

questions.q: Negative feedback in homeostasis works by:
options: Reinforcing a change so it grows larger
Detecting a change and triggering a response that reverses it back to normal
questions.explain: Negative feedback reverses changes: if a level rises too high, a response lowers it back towards the normal value.

questions.q: Type 1 diabetes is caused by:
options: The pancreas not producing enough (or any) insulin
The kidneys failing to filter glucose
The body's cells not responding to insulin
questions.explain: In Type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.q: In dim light, the pupil reflex causes the:
options: Pupil to get larger to let more light in
questions.explain: In dim light radial muscles contract and the pupil widens to let more light reach the retina.

questions.q: A couple are using IVF. FSH and LH may be given to the woman first in order to:
options: Stimulate the maturation and release of several eggs
questions.explain: In IVF, FSH and LH stimulate the ovaries to mature several eggs, which are then collected and fertilised.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: The relay neurone in the spinal cord
A muscle or gland that produces the response
The receptor that detects the stimulus
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: Compared with a conscious response, a spinal reflex is:
options: Faster because it bypasses conscious brain processing
Slower and decided by the brain
The same speed but uses more neurones
questions.explain: Reflexes are faster than conscious responses because they do not pass through the conscious brain.

questions.q: A plant shoot grows towards light. This response is called:
questions.explain: Growth towards light is positive phototropism, controlled by the hormone auxin.

questions.q: What two organs make up the central nervous system (CNS)?
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, which coordinate the body's responses.

questions.q: Reflex actions are described as automatic because they:
options: Do not involve the conscious areas of the brain
Are controlled consciously by the brain
questions.explain: Reflexes are automatic and rapid, not involving conscious thought, which helps protect the body.

questions.q: Light entering the eye is first refracted (bent) by the:
questions.explain: The transparent cornea does most of the refraction of light as it enters the eye.
